NASB.1: Now a certain woman of the wives of the sons of the prophets cried out to Elisha, 'Your servant my husband is dead, and you know that your servant feared the LORD; and the creditor has come to take my two children to be his slaves.'
NASB.2: Elisha said to her, 'What shall I do for you? Tell me, what do you have in the house?' And she said, 'Your maidservant has nothing in the house except a jar of oil.'
NASB.3: Then he said, 'Go, borrow vessels at large for yourself from all your neighbors, [even] empty vessels; do not get a few.
NASB.4: 'And you shall go in and shut the door behind you and your sons, and pour out into all these vessels, and you shall set aside what is full.'
NASB.5: So she went from him and shut the door behind her and her sons; they were bringing [the vessels] to her and she poured.

NASB.8: Now there came a day when Elisha passed over to Shunem, where there was a prominent woman, and she persuaded him to eat food. And so it was, as often as he passed by, he turned in there to eat food.
NASB.9: She said to her husband, 'Behold now, I perceive that this is a holy man of God passing by us continually.
NASB.10: 'Please, let us make a little walled upper chamber and let us set a bed for him there, and a table and a chair and a lampstand; and it shall be, when he comes to us, [that] he can turn in there.'
NASB.11: One day he came there and turned in to the upper chamber and rested.

NASB.13: He said to him, 'Say now to her, 'Behold, you have been careful for us with all this care; what can I do for you? Would you be spoken for to the king or to the captain of the army?'' And she answered, 'I live among my own people.'

NASB.15: He said, 'Call her.' When he had called her, she stood in the doorway.

NASB.24: Then she saddled a donkey and said to her servant, 'Drive and go forward; do not slow down the pace for me unless I tell you.'

NLT.1: One day the widow of a member of the group of prophets came to Elisha and cried out, “My husband who served you is dead, and you know how he feared the LORD. But now a creditor has come, threatening to take my two sons as slaves.”

NLT.4: Then go into your house with your sons and shut the door behind you. Pour olive oil from your flask into the jars, setting each one aside when it is filled.”
NLT.5: So she did as she was told. Her sons kept bringing jars to her, and she filled one after another.
NLT.6: Soon every container was full to the brim! “Bring me another jar,” she said to one of her sons. “There aren’t any more!” he told her. And then the olive oil stopped flowing.
NLT.7: When she told the man of God what had happened, he said to her, “Now sell the olive oil and pay your debts, and you and your sons can live on what is left over.”

NLT.11: One day Elisha returned to Shunem, and he went up to this upper room to rest.

NLT.13: Elisha said to Gehazi, “Tell her, ‘We appreciate the kind concern you have shown us. What can we do for you? Can we put in a good word for you to the king or to the commander of the army?’” “No,” she replied, “my family takes good care of me.”
NLT.14: Later Elisha asked Gehazi, “What can we do for her?” Gehazi replied, “She doesn’t have a son, and her husband is an old man.”
NLT.15: “Call her back again,” Elisha told him. When the woman returned, Elisha said to her as she stood in the doorway,

NLT.19: Suddenly he cried out, “My head hurts! My head hurts!” His father said to one of the servants, “Carry him home to his mother.”
NLT.20: So the servant took him home, and his mother held him on her lap. But around noontime he died.
NLT.21: She carried him up and laid him on the bed of the man of God, then shut the door and left him there.

NLT.23: “Why go today?” he asked. “It is neither a new moon festival nor a Sabbath.” But she said, “It will be all right.”
NLT.24: So she saddled the donkey and said to the servant, “Hurry! Don’t slow down unless I tell you to.”

NLT.28: Then she said, “Did I ask you for a son, my lord? And didn’t I say, ‘Don’t deceive me and get my hopes up’?”
NLT.29: Then Elisha said to Gehazi, “Get ready to travel ; take my staff and go! Don’t talk to anyone along the way. Go quickly and lay the staff on the child’s face.”
NLT.30: But the boy’s mother said, “As surely as the LORD lives and you yourself live, I won’t go home unless you go with me.” So Elisha returned with her.

Gehazi said, "Well, she has no son, and her husband is an old man."
MSG.15: "Call her in," said Elisha. He called her and she stood at the open door.
MSG.16:
Elisha said to her, "This time next year you're going to be nursing an infant son."
"O my master, O Holy Man," she said, "don't play games with me, teasing me with such fantasies!"
MSG.17: The woman conceived. A year later, just as Elisha had said, she had a son.
MSG.18: The child grew up. One day he went to his father, who was working with the harvest hands,
MSG.19:
complaining, "My head, my head!"
His father ordered a servant, "Carry him to his mother."
MSG.20: The servant took him in his arms and carried him to his mother. He lay on her lap until noon and died.
MSG.21: She took him up and laid him on the bed of the man of God, shut him in alone, and left.
MSG.22: She then called her husband, "Get me a servant and a donkey so I can go to the Holy Man; I'll be back as soon as I can."
MSG.23:
"But why today? This isn't a holy day—it's neither New Moon nor Sabbath."
She said, "Don't ask questions; I need to go right now. Trust me."
MSG.24: She went ahead and saddled the donkey, ordering her servant, "Take the lead—and go as fast as you can; I'll tell you if you're going too fast."
MSG.25:
And so off she went. She came to the Holy Man at Mount Carmel.
The Holy Man, spotting her while she was still a long way off, said to his servant Gehazi, "Look out there; why, it's the Shunammite woman!
MSG.26:
Quickly now. Ask her, 'Is something wrong? Are you all right? Your husband? Your child?' "
She said, "Everything's fine."
MSG.27:
But when she reached the Holy Man at the mountain, she threw herself at his feet and held tightly to him.
Gehazi came up to pull her away, but the Holy Man said, "Leave her alone—can't you see that she's in distress? But God hasn't let me in on why; I'm completely in the dark."
MSG.28: Then she spoke up: "Did I ask for a son, master? Didn't I tell you, 'Don't tease me with false hopes'?"
MSG.29: He ordered Gehazi, "Don't lose a minute—grab my staff and run as fast as you can. If you meet anyone, don't even take time to greet him, and if anyone greets you, don't even answer. Lay my staff across the boy's face."
MSG.30: The boy's mother said, "As sure as God lives and you live, you're not leaving me behind." And so Gehazi let her take the lead, and followed behind.
MSG.31: But Gehazi arrived first and laid the staff across the boy's face. But there was no sound—no sign of life. Gehazi went back to meet Elisha and said, "The boy hasn't stirred."
MSG.32: Elisha entered the house and found the boy stretched out on the bed dead.
MSG.33: He went into the room and locked the door—just the two of them in the room—and prayed to God.
MSG.34: He then got into bed with the boy and covered him with his body, mouth on mouth, eyes on eyes, hands on hands. As he was stretched out over him like that, the boy's body became warm.
MSG.35: Elisha got up and paced back and forth in the room. Then he went back and stretched himself upon the boy again. The boy started sneezing—seven times he sneezed!—and opened his eyes.
MSG.36:
He called Gehazi and said, "Get the Shunammite woman in here!" He called her and she came in.
Elisha said, "Embrace your son!"
MSG.37: She fell at Elisha's feet, face to the ground in reverent awe. Then she embraced her son and went out with him.
MSG.38: Elisha went back down to Gilgal. There was a famine there. While he was consulting with the guild of prophets, he told his servant, "Put a large pot on the fire and cook up some stew for the prophets."
MSG.39: One of the men went out into the field to get some herbs; he came across a wild vine and picked gourds from it, filling his gunnysack. He brought them back, sliced them up, and put them in the stew, even though no one knew what kind of plant it was.
MSG.40: The stew was then served up for the men to eat. They started to eat, and then exclaimed, "Death in the pot, O man of God! Death in the pot!" Nobody could eat it.
MSG.41:
Elisha ordered, "Get me some meal." Then he sprinkled it into the stew pot.
"Now serve it up to the men," he said. They ate it, and it was just fine—nothing wrong with that stew!
MSG.42:
One day a man arrived from Baal Shalishah. He brought the man of God twenty loaves of fresh baked bread from the early harvest, along with a few apples from the orchard.
Elisha said, "Pass it around to the people to eat."
MSG.43:
His servant said, "For a hundred men? There's not nearly enough!"
Elisha said, "Just go ahead and do it. God says there's plenty."
MSG.44: And sure enough, there was. He passed around what he had—they not only ate, but had leftovers.

NRSVCE.1: Now the wife of a member of the company of prophets cried to Elisha, “Your servant my husband is dead; and you know that your servant feared the LORD, but a creditor has come to take my two children as slaves.”
NRSVCE.2: Elisha said to her, “What shall I do for you? Tell me, what do you have in the house?” She answered, “Your servant has nothing in the house, except a jar of oil.”
NRSVCE.3: He said, “Go outside, borrow vessels from all your neighbors, empty vessels and not just a few.
NRSVCE.4: Then go in, and shut the door behind you and your children, and start pouring into all these vessels; when each is full, set it aside.”
NRSVCE.5: So she left him and shut the door behind her and her children; they kept bringing vessels to her, and she kept pouring.
NRSVCE.6: When the vessels were full, she said to her son, “Bring me another vessel.” But he said to her, “There are no more.” Then the oil stopped flowing.
NRSVCE.7: She came and told the man of God, and he said, “Go sell the oil and pay your debts, and you and your children can live on the rest.”
NRSVCE.8: One day Elisha was passing through Shunem, where a wealthy woman lived, who urged him to have a meal. So whenever he passed that way, he would stop there for a meal.
NRSVCE.9: She said to her husband, “Look, I am sure that this man who regularly passes our way is a holy man of God.
NRSVCE.10: Let us make a small roof chamber with walls, and put there for him a bed, a table, a chair, and a lamp, so that he can stay there whenever he comes to us.”
NRSVCE.11: One day when he came there, he went up to the chamber and lay down there.
NRSVCE.12: He said to his servant Gehazi, “Call the Shunammite woman.” When he had called her, she stood before him.
NRSVCE.13: He said to him, “Say to her, Since you have taken all this trouble for us, what may be done for you? Would you have a word spoken on your behalf to the king or to the commander of the army?” She answered, “I live among my own people.”
NRSVCE.14: He said, “What then may be done for her?” Gehazi answered, “Well, she has no son, and her husband is old.”
NRSVCE.15: He said, “Call her.” When he had called her, she stood at the door.
NRSVCE.16: He said, “At this season, in due time, you shall embrace a son.” She replied, “No, my lord, O man of God; do not deceive your servant.”
NRSVCE.17: The woman conceived and bore a son at that season, in due time, as Elisha had declared to her.
NRSVCE.18: When the child was older, he went out one day to his father among the reapers.
NRSVCE.19: He complained to his father, “Oh, my head, my head!” The father said to his servant, “Carry him to his mother.”
NRSVCE.20: He carried him and brought him to his mother; the child sat on her lap until noon, and he died.
NRSVCE.21: She went up and laid him on the bed of the man of God, closed the door on him, and left.
NRSVCE.22: Then she called to her husband, and said, “Send me one of the servants and one of the donkeys, so that I may quickly go to the man of God and come back again.”
NRSVCE.23: He said, “Why go to him today? It is neither new moon nor sabbath.” She said, “It will be all right.”
NRSVCE.24: Then she saddled the donkey and said to her servant, “Urge the animal on; do not hold back for me unless I tell you.”
NRSVCE.25: So she set out, and came to the man of God at Mount Carmel. When the man of God saw her coming, he said to Gehazi his servant, “Look, there is the Shunammite woman;
NRSVCE.26: run at once to meet her, and say to her, Are you all right? Is your husband all right? Is the child all right?” She answered, “It is all right.”
NRSVCE.27: When she came to the man of God at the mountain, she caught hold of his feet. Gehazi approached to push her away. But the man of God said, “Let her alone, for she is in bitter distress; the LORD has hidden it from me and has not told me.”
NRSVCE.28: Then she said, “Did I ask my lord for a son? Did I not say, Do not mislead me?”
NRSVCE.29: He said to Gehazi, “Gird up your loins, and take my staff in your hand, and go. If you meet anyone, give no greeting, and if anyone greets you, do not answer; and lay my staff on the face of the child.”
NRSVCE.30: Then the mother of the child said, “As the LORD lives, and as you yourself live, I will not leave without you.” So he rose up and followed her.
NRSVCE.31: Gehazi went on ahead and laid the staff on the face of the child, but there was no sound or sign of life. He came back to meet him and told him, “The child has not awakened.”
NRSVCE.32: When Elisha came into the house, he saw the child lying dead on his bed.
NRSVCE.33: So he went in and closed the door on the two of them, and prayed to the LORD.
NRSVCE.34: Then he got up on the bed and lay upon the child, putting his mouth upon his mouth, his eyes upon his eyes, and his hands upon his hands; and while he lay bent over him, the flesh of the child became warm.
NRSVCE.35: He got down, walked once to and fro in the room, then got up again and bent over him; the child sneezed seven times, and the child opened his eyes.
NRSVCE.36: Elisha summoned Gehazi and said, “Call the Shunammite woman.” So he called her. When she came to him, he said, “Take your son.”
NRSVCE.37: She came and fell at his feet, bowing to the ground; then she took her son and left.
NRSVCE.38: When Elisha returned to Gilgal, there was a famine in the land. As the company of prophets was sitting before him, he said to his servant, “Put the large pot on, and make some stew for the company of prophets.”
NRSVCE.39: One of them went out into the field to gather herbs; he found a wild vine and gathered from it a lapful of wild gourds, and came and cut them up into the pot of stew, not knowing what they were.
NRSVCE.40: They served some for the men to eat. But while they were eating the stew, they cried out, “O man of God, there is death in the pot!” They could not eat it.
NRSVCE.41: He said, “Then bring some flour.” He threw it into the pot, and said, “Serve the people and let them eat.” And there was nothing harmful in the pot.
NRSVCE.42: A man came from Baal-shalishah, bringing food from the first fruits to the man of God: twenty loaves of barley and fresh ears of grain in his sack. Elisha said, “Give it to the people and let them eat.”
NRSVCE.43: But his servant said, “How can I set this before a hundred people?” So he repeated, “Give it to the people and let them eat, for thus says the LORD, ‘They shall eat and have some left.’”
NRSVCE.44: He set it before them, they ate, and had some left, according to the word of the LORD.
